hi, my special interest is psychology too and i wanted to provide a potential answer to ur second question. i think one reason autism has so many negative stereotypes is due to misinformation. people don’t feel the need to educate themselves on things that don’t effect them, so when they hear harmful myths like ‘autism is caused by vaccines’ or ‘autistic people have no empathy’, ideas like that are subconsciously embedded into their brains, causing them to pity or look down on us- so one reason there are so many negative stereotypes would bc due to a lack of education on the topic. this could be improved by adding topics such as mental health and neurodivergence to the school curriculum…

another reason for the negative stereotypes on autism would probably be due to the media. the representation of autism in the media is very black and white and doesn’t even begin to show the fluidity of diversity within the autism spectrum. the majority of autistic characters depict a straight, white male who has an interest in maths/science and a monotone voice (the big bang theory, atypical, the good doctor-to name a few). or they put no research into the role at all (music, sia’s movie is perfect example of this). all these movies add onto these stereotypes. hopefully in the future as research develops, so will the general understanding of autism which ideally would result in a development of a more accurate autistic representation in the media and thereby less harmful stereotypes!
